p05: Create NEW four Hypericum perforatum organs as a botanically accurate 2x2 educational raster sheet, Fronda graphic style from reference: bold smooth dark-brown outlines, flat green/cream/yellow fills, restrained shading. Genuine transparent alpha, no text or arrows/frames/shadows. All four illustrations wholly separated within own quadrants with ample transparent padding. TOP LEFT: one complete SIMPLE Hypericum leaf, oval-elliptic to oblong, about 2.5times longer than wide, rounded apex and tapered sessile base, smooth entire margin, pale cream midrib and a few side veins. Tiny translucent pale dots scattered in blade and a few small dark gland dots close to its edge, as documented, not holes or serrations. No long petiole. TOP RIGHT: enlarged portion of the SAME leaf EDGE, a curved absolutely SMOOTH entire green border with a few tiny dark gland dots just inside and pale translucent dots in blade, no teeth, no spines, no notch. Only a cropped blade portion. BOTTOM LEFT: single Hypericum flower from front, exactly FIVE slightly asymmetric golden YELLOW oblong petals radiating with a subtle pinwheel arrangement, small dark gland dots near petal tips, MANY slender yellow stamens centrally grouped in three subtle bundles, no daisy disk and no extra petals. Small green pointed sepals behind barely visible. BOTTOM RIGHT: exterior view of ONE CLOSED Hypericum capsule, ovate conical body with three seams, three thin persistent style remnants at apex, small five slender calyx lobes at base, short stalk. Render this capsule ONLY in neutral cream fill and dark-brown contour with cream shading, no green or red fruit color: color is intentionally NOT represented because catalog fruit color is undocumented. No opening valves or loose seeds. Based on actual University of Trieste closed capsule photo IMG7216JPG1596122945 and Flora Helvetica2018. No leaf or flower appended to capsule.
p06: NEW four-organ 2x2 botanical educational sprite sheet, clean Fronda graphic style: dark brown bold outlines, flat green/cream/lilac fills, no texture except simple veins. True transparent alpha, generous padding and gutters, no text/arrows/frames/shadows. TOP LEFT: one complete SIMPLE Silene vulgaris leaf, oval-lanceolate narrow blade, acute tip, smooth straight entire margins, pale central vein, sessile tapering base, no long petiole, no teeth or hairs, about 4 times longer than wide. TOP RIGHT: ONE Silene vulgaris flower shown three-quarter side/front, swollen oval bladder-like PALE GREEN CALYX with a delicate reddish-brown vein network, corolla emerging from its mouth with exactly FIVE WHITE petals, each petal deeply split into TWO narrow rounded lobes (ten visible petal tips grouped as five pairs), no extra petals. Slim green stalk. It must show inflated calyx as well as white bifid petals, not a flat rose blossom. BOTTOM LEFT: ONE Silene vulgaris mature OPEN capsule in slightly oblique top view, rounded-ovoid small body in neutral cream, dark-brown contours, open terminal circular mouth with EXACTLY SIX short triangular teeth, empty dark interior with no loose seeds. A little remnant of papery enclosing calyx on one side and thin short stalk. Neutral diagram colors only, do not imply exact fruit color. Match University of Trieste open-capsule photo IMG6910JPG1596103683. BOTTOM RIGHT: ONE Campanula rapunculus flower, light LILAC open bell-shaped corolla, narrow base and flaring mouth divided into FIVE pointed triangular lobes almost halfway down bell, five thin green linear calyx lobes beneath, pale style gently projecting at mouth. One slim stalk, no extra leaves. Bell is open, not closed inflated tube or lily. Verified morphology Flora Helvetica2018 and real species photos.
p07: NEW 2x2 botanical educational raster sheet with four isolated drawings, exact Fronda clean style as reference: bold smooth dark-brown contour, flat green fills, a few cream veins, no phototexture. True transparent alpha everywhere outside shapes. No text, no arrows/frames/shadows. Each drawing entirely within quadrant, generous transparent gutters and margins. TOP LEFT: ONE complete simple Campanula rapunculus LOWER/basal leaf, elongated oblong-obovate blade, about 4times longer than wide, widest in upper half, broadly acute or obtuse tip, blade attenuated gradually toward a short narrow petiole, sparse SMALL SHALLOW widely spaced teeth along side margins, not exaggerated serrations and not lobed. Light cream midrib, 5-6 thin side veins, only a few tiny soft hairs. TOP RIGHT: enlarged portion of same rapunculus leaf EDGE, almost smooth gently curved green blade with 4 small low pointed teeth widely separated by long smooth stretches, a few pale lateral veins and fine soft hairs; only edge portion, not a whole leaf. BOTTOM LEFT: ONE complete simple Primula vulgaris leaf, obovate-oblong blade, about 2.5times longer than wide, rounded apex, broad upper third, base gradually narrowed into a short broad winged petiole, finely irregular crenate-dentate margin, noticeably wrinkled reticulate venation represented with SIMPLE cream main and cross veins rather than realistic bumpy texture. Leaf margin teeth are shallow and rounded, not lobes or spines. BOTTOM RIGHT: enlarged fragment of primrose margin showing small irregular rounded/crenate teeth plus a few sharper low teeth and reticulate veins; only blade portion. The drawings should clearly distinguish sparse shallow rapunculus teeth from densely crenate primrose margin. Real species reference leaves from University of Trieste IMG5563 and TSB42911; supporting Flora Helvetica / NC State species descriptions.
